method: Fetched each URL with curl (browser or declared research User-Agent; SEC requires a declared agent) into an isolated temp directory, stripped HTML/converted PDF with pdftotext -layout, and located the exact passage for each chapter claim. Kaggle live pages returned a reCAPTCHA challenge, so the preserved API metadata in data/historical/kaggle-metadata.json and kaggle-listing.json was read instead. Two additional primary/secondary records (Apple Q1 FY16 release; Nasdaq AAPL/MSFT dividend history) were consulted only to test a reviewer finding about dividend adjustment; they are not chapter sources.

checks.claim: Chapter's 'under the 2016 settlement cycle the shares went ex-dividend on February 4'. The page describes only the current convention, not the 2016 two-business-day rule; the February 4 date itself is supported by the Nasdaq dividend-history check above.

boundaries: Revision re-check: the chapter now lists eight source records. Fourteen checks cover them over eight URLs (one Kaggle live retrieval failed; preserved metadata used). Three further checks over three URLs support or attempt to test a reviewer finding and are not chapter sources. Partial: the SEC report says 'closing price' without stating 'regular-session' (the official close is conventionally the regular-session close; wording could say 'reported closing prices'); the Kaggle description gives a last-update date (11/10/2017) that bounds the adjustment vintage although the formula remains undocumented. Fictional cases have no source by design. Edition-wide rights review (ROAD-003) is out of scope; nothing alarming beyond the already-disclosed limits of a depositor-asserted CC0 on vendor-origin market data. Retrieval failure is not evidence of an unsupported claim. Revision note: the 2016 two-business-day ex-date convention is not stated in any fetched page; the ex-date is nonetheless supported by Nasdaq's AAPL dividend history (ex 02/04/2016, record 02/08/2016). The revised wording 'Reported closing prices' and the bounded vintage note resolve the two earlier partial dispositions in the chapter text.
